samples.summary: The lapse value CollabDocumentProvider computes (unsupported / not-permitted / not-enabled / another-tab) is never asserted by any test
samples.evidence: `collab-document-provider.tsx` derives `lapse` from `supportsClientKey()`, `permitted`, `offlineEnabled` and the election, and publishes it via `DurabilityLapseScope`. Every test that exercises lapse behaviour injects the value by hand: `tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx:632` and `:865` wrap the chip in `<DurabilityLapseScope lapse={...}>` directly, and `sync-status-tooltip.ts` is tested as a pure function. Grepping `lapse|Lapse` across `src/components/__tests__` returns nothing (only an unrelated loader comment), and the two durable provider suites (`collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx`, `collab-document-provider-identity.test.tsx`) assert only `clientKey`/`store`/mount counts. So the mapping from provider state to cause is uncovered: if it collapsed to `not-permitted`, the chip's `offerOffline` (`sync-status-chip.tsx:84`, `lapse !== 'not-permitted'`) would silently disappear on every non-durable document — the design's second entry point for turning the feature on — and no test would fail. (Impact is currently deferred because `@yorkie-js/react` is pinned to 0.7.22 so `supportsClientKey()` is false, but the gap ships permanently and goes live on a one-line bump.)

samples.summary: DurableYorkieProvider's published lapse (dropped / too-large / out-of-space / write-failed / unreportable) is untested; the quota branch is never driven
samples.evidence: `durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx` asserts only the `durable` boolean through `useDocumentDurability()` (the `Probe` at line ~200 renders 'durable'/'not-durable'); nothing reads `useDurabilityLapse()` in that suite. The `out-of-space` value depends on `onWriteFailure` receiving a `DOMException(..., 'QuotaExceededError')` (`durable-yorkie-provider.tsx` onWriteFailure), but every case calls `captured[0].onWriteFailure?.(new Error('refused'))`, which only exercises the generic `write-failed` path. A wrong precedence or a missed quota classification would show the user the wrong remedy in the tooltip with no failing test.

samples.summary: An existing traversal guard is weakened from 'every request carries the encoded id' to 'some request does'
samples.evidence: The loop previously asserted `expect(pathname).toContain(encodeURIComponent(TRAVERSAL))` for every URL a call produced; it now asserts only `paths.some(...)`. The remaining per-URL check is `not.toContain('/auth/logout')`, which catches raw interpolation only when the traversal normalizes into that path. A companion request that embedded the id unencoded somewhere that does not normalize to `/auth/logout` (a query string, a different segment depth) now passes, because the primary request supplies the `some` match. The relaxation was introduced to accommodate `deleteWorkspace`'s new `fetchDocuments()` companion call, which could have been excused more narrowly (e.g. only ignoring paths that contain no id at all).

samples.summary: belongsToAnotherUser (cross-account orphan-snapshot skip in collectStale) has no test; the only orphan test uses a key shape production never writes
samples.evidence: `collectStale` collects orphan snapshot rows filtered by `!this.belongsToAnotherUser(docKey)` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1295). The only orphan test is `wafflebase-doc-store-atomicity.test.ts:112` ('is collected rather than living forever out of reach'), which seeds `doc-a` — a key with no `wb:{secret}:{userId}:` segment, so the regex matches nothing and the branch is never taken. Real store keys are always `apiKey/wb:{secret}:{userId}:{docKey}/{docKey}`, so the production shape is untested in both directions: no case proves this user's own `wb:`-keyed orphan is still collected, and none proves another account's is skipped. A regex bug making it match this user's own keys would leave every real orphan permanently uncollectable — document content that neither the sweep nor logout can reach.

samples.summary: The keepArchives option on dropAllForUser / eraseOfflineData has no caller and no test
samples.evidence: `dropAllForUser(userId, { keepArchives })` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts:1123,1161) and `eraseOfflineData(store, userId, { keepArchives })` (offline-erase.ts:30) are documented at length as being 'for the one caller that did not ask for any of this' — but grepping `keepArchives` across `packages/frontend/src` returns only those definitions: `api/auth.ts` now passes `eraseLocalData: 'none'` on the 401 arm, so nothing ever erases-but-keeps-archives. No test passes the option either, so the documented behaviour (live entries dropped, archives preserved) is unexercised and its claim unverifiable.
searchedFor: read api/auth.ts logout arm in diff

samples.summary: No test covers the retraction/confirmation path out of the new saved-locally toast
samples.evidence: The new `savedLocally` arm sets `warned.current = true` (sync-status-chip.tsx:190) expressly so the recovery arm below retracts the info toast and confirms once the work reaches the server. The durable section of `tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx` ('says where the work went instead of saying nothing') only asserts `toast.info` fired; no case transitions a durable document from `saved-locally` to `saved` and asserts `dismiss(TOAST_ID)` plus the `Saved` success toast. The pre-existing recovery tests (lines ~373-403) drive the `not-saved` path only, so a regression that left the info toast pinned or skipped the confirmation would pass.
searchedFor: read the durable describe block of the chip test

samples.summary: The advisory touch-on-load write (cross-instance liveness) is not asserted anywhere
samples.evidence: `load()` calls `void this.touch(docKey)` (wafflebase-doc-store.ts ~528) specifically so a document opened but not yet edited is visible as recently used to *other* store instances, which `touched` (per-instance memory) cannot convey. The cleanup suite's cross-instance cases all inject `isOpenElsewhere` instead (`wafflebase-doc-store-cleanup.test.ts:535-620`), and the single-instance case ('never evicts a document this session has open, even the oldest one') passes purely via the in-memory `touched` set. So no test would fail if `touch()` were removed, even though a document opened in another tab without a lock answer would then be the first eviction/collection candidate.
searchedFor: read wafflebase-doc-store-cleanup.test.ts eviction and 'documents open in another tab' sections

samples.summary: The promise that local purge can never fail an accepted deletion is untested at both levels
samples.evidence: `deleteDocument` awaits `purgeOfflineDocuments([id])` on the success path with the comment 'never able to turn an accepted deletion into a reported failure' (documents.ts:163-166). `documents.test.ts` mocks `purgeOfflineDocuments` wholesale and never makes it reject, and `offline-erase.test.ts`'s 'a document that was deleted' block has no case where the underlying store throws. So nothing pins that a purge failure is swallowed rather than surfacing as a failed delete to the user.
searchedFor: read src/lib/offline-erase.test.ts 'a document that was deleted' describe

samples.summary: The 'is the route saying so, not the default' case renders the mocked provider, so it asserts the context default rather than the real provider
samples.evidence: The file mocks `@/components/collab-document-provider` (line 24) with a probe span, then imports and renders that same mocked component at line 87 and asserts it reads `true`. The comment ('Durability is permitted by default — every owned editor depends on that') implies the real `CollabDocumentProvider` is exercised; it is not — the assertion only shows `DurabilityPermitted`'s default outside any scope. It is still useful as a control for the first case, but it proves nothing about owned editors.

finding.summary: The lapse value CollabDocumentProvider computes (unsupported / not-permitted / not-enabled / another-tab) is never asserted by any test
finding.evidence: `collab-document-provider.tsx` derives `lapse` from `supportsClientKey()`, `permitted`, `offlineEnabled` and the election, and publishes it via `DurabilityLapseScope`. Every test that exercises lapse behaviour injects the value by hand: `tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx:632` and `:865` wrap the chip in `<DurabilityLapseScope lapse={...}>` directly, and `sync-status-tooltip.ts` is tested as a pure function. Grepping `lapse|Lapse` across `src/components/__tests__` returns nothing (only an unrelated loader comment), and the two durable provider suites (`collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx`, `collab-document-provider-identity.test.tsx`) assert only `clientKey`/`store`/mount counts. So the mapping from provider state to cause is uncovered: if it collapsed to `not-permitted`, the chip's `offerOffline` (`sync-status-chip.tsx:84`, `lapse !== 'not-permitted'`) would silently disappear on every non-durable document — the design's second entry point for turning the feature on — and no test would fail. (Impact is currently deferred because `@yorkie-js/react` is pinned to 0.7.22 so `supportsClientKey()` is false, but the gap ships permanently and goes live on a one-line bump.)

verdict.reason: The lapse derivation in CollabDocumentProvider (collab-document-provider.tsx:291-299, published at :350) is genuinely untested. A repo-wide word-boundary grep for `\blapse\b|DurabilityLapse` across ts/tsx/js/mjs returns only 7 files, of which just one is a test — tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx — and that suite injects the value by hand (renderWithLapse at :625-634, strandedUnderScopes at :857-869) rather than rendering the provider; its only mention of CollabDocumentProvider is a prose comment at :847. All three provider suites (collab-document-provider.test.tsx presence-repair cases :86-213, -durable.test.tsx :154-540 asserting clientKey/store/mount counts/locks, -identity.test.tsx) contain no lapse reference; grep for `durable-document-context|Scope|lapse` under src/components/__tests__ yields only NonDurableScope imports. No test calls useDurabilityLapse() (only sync-status-chip.tsx:79 does), and shared-document-durability.test.tsx:24-31 mocks CollabDocumentProvider away entirely, probing useDurabilityPermitted instead. I additionally searched for the user-facing reason strings from sync-status-tooltip.ts:29-40 repo-wide and for any e2e specs; the only hits are the same chip suite (pure tooltipFor / injected scopes) and docs. So the mapping from provider state to cause — which gates offerOffline at sync-status-chip.tsx:95-99 via `lapse !== 'not-permitted'` — could collapse and no test would fail. Under the test-adequacy lens this is a changed behavior with no meaningful test; deferred impact (supportsClientKey pinned false) affects severity grading, not whether the gap is real.

finding.summary: `purgeOfflineDocuments`'s `dropArchives` option is never exercised against the real implementation, so the archive-purge on lost workspace access is uncovered
finding.evidence: `api/workspaces.ts:136,167` call `purgeOfflineDocuments(doomed, { dropArchives: true })` — the mechanism that removes archived full-document snapshots when a workspace is deleted or the signed-in member is removed. `workspaces.test.ts:15-16` mocks `@/lib/offline-erase` wholesale, so its five `expect(mockPurge).toHaveBeenCalledWith([...], { dropArchives: true })` assertions only prove the argument is forwarded to a stub. `offline-erase.test.ts`'s "a document that was deleted" block (lines 667-703) is the only place the real `purgeOfflineDocuments` runs, and every call there omits the option (`purgeOfflineDocuments(["abc"])`, `(["keep"])`, `(["anon"])`); one of them asserts the *opposite* ("keeps the archives", line 680). Grep for `dropArchives` across `packages/frontend/src` returns only the two call sites, the mocked assertions, and the two lines of the implementation. If the `options.dropArchives ? "drop" : "keep"` mapping at offline-erase.ts:405 were wrong, archives of a workspace the user was removed from would stay on disk and `recoverOfflineCopy` would re-materialize that content as a document the user owns — the exact privacy rule the feature states — with every suite green.

verdict.reason: Verified independently and found no counterexample. Repo-wide grep for `dropArchives` yields only the two call sites (api/workspaces.ts:136,167), the five mocked assertions in api/workspaces.test.ts (85,99,108,148,164), and the implementation (offline-erase.ts:395,405). Repo-wide grep for `purgeOfflineDocuments` shows the real function is invoked only at offline-erase.test.ts:675,690,700, every call with a single array argument and no options; line 680-692 in fact asserts the opposite branch ("keeps the archives"). Indirect routes are closed: api/workspaces.test.ts:14-16 mocks @/lib/offline-erase wholesale, app/workspaces/__tests__/workspace-settings.test.tsx:28-36 mocks @/api/workspaces wholesale so deleteWorkspace/removeMember never execute, and tests/api/auth.test.ts:87 also mocks the module; nothing under packages/frontend/tests/** (388 files) or any other package references the option. Mitigation exists but is not a counterexample: wafflebase-doc-store-cleanup.test.ts:708-718 and 915-971 cover the real store.purgeDocument(..., {archives:"drop"}), so both ends of the chain are tested while the joining mapping at offline-erase.ts:405 and the end-to-end "lost workspace access ⇒ archives removed" behavior are covered by no test. If that ternary were inverted, archives of a workspace the user was removed from would survive and recovery would re-materialize them, with the whole suite green — a silent weakening of a stated privacy guard, squarely a missing-test finding in the test-adequacy lane.

finding.summary: No test renders the real lapse publishers, so which `DurabilityLapse` each one emits — and which scope wins when both are mounted — is uncovered
finding.evidence: `useDurabilityLapse` has exactly two producers: `collab-document-provider.tsx:350` (`unsupported`/`not-permitted`/`not-enabled`/`another-tab`) and `durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:238` (`dropped`/`too-large`/`out-of-space`/`write-failed`/`unreportable`). Grepping `DurabilityLapseScope|useDurabilityLapse` across packages/frontend shows the only test usage is `tests/components/sync-status/sync-status-chip.test.tsx:632,865-869`, which hand-mounts the scopes with literal lapse values. So every "tooltip names which case applies" assertion (lines 783-841) and the `strandedUnderScopes` block (845-880) passes regardless of what the production components compute. Concretely uncovered: (a) the nesting order at collab-document-provider.tsx:350 — the comment there records that this scope was once mounted *inside* `inner`, which silently swallowed every durable-client reason; re-inverting it today fails no test, because the chip test supplies its own correctly-ordered scopes; (b) `durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:164-169`, the `QuotaExceededError → setOutOfSpace(true)` branch, whose only observable effect is the `out-of-space` lapse — `durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx` fires `onWriteFailure(new Error('refused'))` and asserts only `useDocumentDurability()`, never the lapse; (c) that the share-link route actually publishes `not-permitted`, which is what the chip's offer-suppression (`sync-status-chip.tsx:99`) keys on.

verdict.reason: Searched repo-wide (not just the reviewer's paths) and found no test that renders either real lapse publisher and asserts the DurabilityLapse it computes. The only test references to DurabilityLapseScope are sync-status-chip.test.tsx:632 and :865-869, which hand-mount the scope with literal lapse values, so the chip assertions pass regardless of what collab-document-provider.tsx:291-299 or durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:215-225 actually compute. collab-document-provider-durable.test.tsx does render the real provider but asserts only clientKey/store/election/loss-watch, never a lapse. shared-document-durability.test.tsx mocks CollabDocumentProvider away and asserts only useDurabilityPermitted(), so the share-link -> 'not-permitted' lapse is untested. durable-yorkie-provider.test.tsx imports only useDocumentDurability (line 66, probe line 94) and asserts durable/not-durable, so the QuotaExceededError -> setOutOfSpace(true) branch (durable-yorkie-provider.tsx:161-171), whose sole observable effect is the 'out-of-space' lapse, would survive deletion. No e2e/Playwright coverage exists (no e2e dir, no frontend *.spec.ts), and no test asserts any of the lapse tooltip sentences outside sync-status-chip.test.tsx. Partial mitigation: the scope's inherit-on-undefined precedence rule is exercised with the real component at sync-status-chip.test.tsx:865-869, which blunts sub-claim (a) somewhat, but the producers' branch-to-lapse mappings remain wholly uncovered — a user-visible diagnostic guard that could silently regress undetected. Blocking under the test-adequacy rubric as a missing test over changed behavior.
